title: Cross-Regime Measurement Failure in the KT3b Environmental Test
description: Analyzes the null result of the KT3b environmental mass-scaling test in Energy-Flow Cosmology and shows that the monotonic signal collapse across increasingly rigorous runs is explained by a cross-regime measurement inconsistency. It identifies explicit violations of the Regime-Consistent Measurement Principle (driver–response mismatch, boundary observation, and mass-model mixing), and proposes three RCMP-consistent test architectures as a methodological diagnosis stronger than the null result itself.
author: Morten Magnusson

effective_density.description: Working KT3b hypothesis: an environmental coupling with strength \alpha adds an L1 environmental term to the L2 galactic effective density.

rar_residual_at_a0.description: The KT3b observable used to probe environmental modulation; it lies on the L1/L2 transition where measurement is intrinsically unstable.

deep_L2_slope.description: Proposed RCMP-consistent L2 observable (Architecture A): the deep-regime RAR slope that should correlate with environment if Deff is environmentally modulated.

cross_regime_kernel.description: Required but undefined L1→L2 coupling operator in KT3b: a scale- and mode-dependent kernel K that maps L1 density fields to L2 dynamical response.

key_results.main_finding: The KT3b signal’s monotonic collapse to null across four increasingly controlled runs is best explained by a cross-regime measurement inconsistency (RCMP violation), not by statistics alone.

sealed_predictions.statement: In a pure L2 architecture, the deep-regime RAR slope S_L2 correlates with environment (e.g., Theta1 or group richness) when evaluated at g_bar/a0 ~ 0.01–0.1, after mass-matching and systematics control.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Re-analysis of SPARC (or deeper samples) measuring S_L2 vs. environment in mass- and radius-matched subsamples with robust systematics control.

kill_criteria: KC1: Architecture A (pure L2) finds no correlation between the deep-regime RAR slope S_L2 and environment (Theta1 or N_mem) at |slope| < 0.01 (95% CI) across a mass- and radius-matched sample of N ≥ 100 galaxies; this falsifies environment-modulated Deff and kills the KT3b-style environmental coupling within EFC.

KC2: Architecture B (pure L1) constrains the L1 growth coupling to alpha_L1 = 0.00 ± 0.05 with no detectable scale or redshift dependence over 0 < z < 1; this rules out the predicted L1 modulation of Γ(ρ) in EFC.

KC3: A derived L1→L2 mapping (Architecture C) yields a specific non-zero α(k, z) whose predicted trend in KT3b-like observables is not observed at ≥ 3σ in mass- and systematics-controlled samples; this falsifies the derived EFC coupling implementation.

target.original_observable: R = g_obs / g_bar at g_bar ~ a_0

regime_assignment.why: Non-linear galactic dynamics; grid-mode activation at g < a_0
Large-scale structure; Mpc-scale density field; linear perturbation theory
Transition point where the regime changes; maximally unstable
Stellar population synthesis assumes universal IMF and standard gravity

rcmp_violations.name: Driver-response mismatch
rcmp_violations.statement: rho_env (L1) drives D_eff (L2) through an underived alpha operator

rcmp_violations.name: Boundary observation
rcmp_violations.statement: R at a_0 sits on the L1/L2 boundary where both regimes contribute and neither dominates; stiffness response R(k), entropy production Gamma(rho), and effective Poisson coupling mu(k) all transition here

rcmp_violations.name: Implicit regime mixing in mass model
rcmp_violations.statement: Upsilon_star = 0.5 M_sun/L_sun assumes L1-regime stellar physics applied to L2-regime gravitational dynamics

issues: alpha not defined as an operator in function space without a scale- and mode-dependent kernel
no scale dependence: the same alpha applies regardless of the spatial scale separating L1 and L2
no mechanism: does not specify how Mpc-scale density affects kpc-scale mode activation
structurally underdetermined: any measured slope could be attributed to alpha, to an L1/L2 projection artefact, or to residual mass-environment correlation

valid_architectures.name: Pure L2 (galactic interior)
valid_architectures.prediction: D_eff modifies the shape of the RAR in the deep-MOND regime (g << a_0), not just its value at a_0
valid_architectures.observable: d log(g_obs/g_bar) / d log g_bar at g_bar << a_0 (deep L2 regime)
valid_architectures.driver: Same Theta_1 or N_mem, but observable safely inside L2
valid_architectures.why_it_works: Measurement point is far from the regime boundary; deep-MOND slope probes a regime where R(k) has saturated (mu >> 1), reducing sensitivity to boundary fluctuations and isolating intrinsic L2 dynamics

valid_architectures.name: Pure L1 (cosmological growth)
valid_architectures.prediction: D_eff enters the cosmological background through Gamma(rho), which controls the growth rate fsigma8(z); environmental density at L1 scales directly modulates Gamma without cross-regime coupling
valid_architectures.observable: fsigma8(z) from RSD or void-cluster growth rate comparison
valid_architectures.why_it_works: Everything is in L1. The MCMC inference pipeline already constrains alpha_L1.

valid_architectures.name: Derived L1->L2 mapping
valid_architectures.requirement: Derive alpha from the EFC action by computing how the background S-field at L1 scales enters the boundary conditions of the L2 Poisson equation
valid_architectures.observable: Same as KT3b, but with a predicted alpha(k, z) rather than a free parameter
valid_architectures.why_it_is_hard: Requires solving the coupled (g_mu_nu, S) system across scales; open problem in EFC

key_findings: KT3b null is consistent with a cross-regime measurement design that violates RCMP, not with a physical absence of environmental coupling
The L1/L2 boundary is the worst place to measure any cross-regime effect
The alpha coupling is not a physical parameter but an effective fit coefficient absorbing all cross-regime effects indiscriminately
Architecture A (pure L2, RAR slope at 10^-2 < g_bar/a_0 < 10^-1) is the recommended immediate next step: existing SPARC data, zero free parameters, single regime

The diagnosis applies to MOND's External Field Effect, Verlinde's emergent gravity, and any framework in which the transition scale a_0 marks a regime boundary — it is stronger than the null result itself
limitations: The analysis is structural, not numerical: it does not re-derive the KT3b slope values, only diagnoses why they collapse
The Fisher-information argument for low S/N at the L1/L2 boundary is qualitative; a quantitative bound requires the full mu(k) fluctuation spectrum
Architecture C is described as an open problem — no explicit path to the derived alpha(k, z) is provided
The package includes no re-analysis of SPARC or Tully group catalogues; it is a methodological paper
